activity: Ammonia compressor operation and routine top-up
hazard_description: Anhydrous ammonia (R-717) release from compressor seal / flange / relief valve on the primary refrigeration circuit
potential_consequence: Acute inhalation injury, chemical burns to eyes and respiratory tract, fatality above IDLH 300 ppm; potential flammable atmosphere at 15-28 vol% in air
existing_controls: Plant room ventilation; annual pressure vessel certificate; operator on shift
additional_controls: Fixed NH3 gas detectors at 25 ppm alarm / 300 ppm trip interlocked to emergency ventilation and compressor shutdown; two SCBA sets plus 4 full-face ammonia cartridge respirators at the plant-room entrance; emergency deluge shower and eye wash within 10 m; NH3-specific ERP with exclusion zoning and wind-direction assembly points; competency licence for refrigeration operators; restricted access
legal_reference: BLR 60 & 62 (pressure plant certificate); BLA 62 (precautions against fire and dangerous fumes); BLA 78A (training)

activity: Maintenance on ammonia lines and valves
hazard_description: Stored pressure and trapped liquid ammonia released during line breaking without isolation or pump-down
potential_consequence: Severe chemical burns, frostbite from liquid NH3, asphyxiation in confined plant room
existing_controls: Verbal isolation instruction to fitters
additional_controls: Written LOTO procedure with unique padlocks and personal danger tags; line-breaking permit requiring pump-down, double block and bleed, and nitrogen purge verification; gas test before and during work; standby person outside the plant room

activity: Entry into chilled and frozen finished-goods store
hazard_description: Cold stress, slips on ice build-up, personnel locked inside, forklift movement in restricted visibility
potential_consequence: Hypothermia, fractures from falls, crush injury, entrapment
existing_controls: Insulated jackets issued; door kept on latch
additional_controls: Internal door-release and emergency alarm inside the store; man-in-store register with time limits; anti-slip flooring and scheduled defrost; pedestrian walkway segregation with mirrors at blind corners

activity: Tipping 25 kg milk-powder bags into blender and hopper
hazard_description: Combustible milk-powder dust cloud in the blender headspace and dust extraction ducting; ignition from static discharge, hot bearing or electrical fault
potential_consequence: Deflagration and secondary dust explosion, structural damage, multiple fatalities and severe burns
existing_controls: Dust extraction at tipping point; housekeeping by sweeping
additional_controls: Dust hazard analysis to NFPA 61; earthing and bonding continuity testing of all conductive plant and operator wrist straps; ATEX/EX-rated electrical fittings and dust-tight luminaires in the classified zone; explosion venting or suppression on the blender and cyclone; ban on compressed-air blow-down, replaced with certified vacuum cleaning; monthly dust-layer inspection above false ceilings and on beams
legal_reference: BLA 62 (precautions in case of fire); BLA 61 (fencing of machinery); BNBC 2020 Part 4

activity: Manual handling of 25 kg raw-material sacks
hazard_description: Repetitive lifting and carrying of heavy sacks at floor level with trunk flexion and twisting
potential_consequence: Lower-back musculoskeletal disorder, chronic disability, lost-time injury
existing_controls: Two-person lift instruction
additional_controls: Scissor-lift tables and vacuum bag lifters at the tipping station; pallet height maintained between knee and shoulder; job rotation every two hours; documented manual-handling training with a lifting-technique assessment; task redesign to bulk-bag (500 kg) feed where volume justifies it

activity: Nitrogen flushing of powder pouches and cans
hazard_description: Oxygen displacement by nitrogen at the sealing head and in low-lying pits or unventilated corners
potential_consequence: Asphyxiation without warning, loss of consciousness and death
existing_controls: Local exhaust at the sealing head
additional_controls: Fixed oxygen depletion monitors with audible/visual alarm at 19.5% O2; portable multi-gas detector for anyone entering pits or ducts; no-lone-working rule near N2 lines; clear labelling and colour-coding of N2 pipework

activity: Operating rotary valves and packing machinery
hazard_description: Unguarded in-running nips at the rotary valve, auger, conveyor and sealing jaw
potential_consequence: Amputation of fingers or hand, crush injury, entanglement
existing_controls: Fixed guards on some units; caution signage
additional_controls: Guard audit against BLA 61 with interlocked guards on all access doors; two-hand controls and emergency stop within reach on every station; LOTO applied to every clearance and cleaning task; guard-removal treated as a permit activity
legal_reference: BLA 61 (fencing of machinery); BLA 63 (self-acting machines); BLR 61

activity: Operation of continuous palm-oil fryer at 140-180 C
hazard_description: Hot-oil fire from thermostat failure, overheating or oil overflow onto burners; fire spread through the extraction canopy and grease-laden ductwork
potential_consequence: Severe full-thickness burns, fatality, total loss of the production hall
existing_controls: Portable CO2 extinguishers; manual temperature gauge
additional_controls: High-temperature cut-out independent of the control thermostat; automatic wet-chemical (Class F) suppression over the fryer and inside the canopy with fuel/gas auto-shutoff; scheduled duct degreasing with records; oil-level low/high alarms; oil-spill containment and non-slip surface around the fryer; ban on water-based extinguishers in the area
legal_reference: BLA 62; Fire Prevention and Extinction Act 2003 ss.4 & 8; BNBC 2020 Part 4

activity: Draining and changing hot frying oil
hazard_description: Contact with oil above 100 C during draining and transfer
potential_consequence: Severe scald burns to hands, arms, legs and face
existing_controls: Long-sleeve uniform; drain when convenient
additional_controls: Mandatory cool-down to below 50 C with a verified temperature reading before draining, recorded on the changeover checklist; closed pumped transfer to a sealed drum instead of open ladling; heat-resistant gauntlets, apron and face shield; exclusion barrier during transfer

activity: Operation of gas-fired tunnel oven
hazard_description: Unburnt natural gas accumulation in the oven chamber from failed ignition, flame failure or leaking train
potential_consequence: Gas explosion, structural collapse of the oven, multiple burn casualties
existing_controls: Manual purge before light-up
additional_controls: Certified burner management system with proven pre-purge, flame-supervision and automatic safety shut-off valves; annual third-party gas-train integrity test; gas detection in the oven bay with automatic isolation; light-up authorised only by a trained and named operator
legal_reference: BLA 62; Fire Prevention and Extinction Act 2003; BNBC 2020 Part 8

activity: Steam boiler operation and blowdown
hazard_description: Pressure-vessel failure, steam release during blowdown, contact with uninsulated steam lines
potential_consequence: Catastrophic vessel rupture, fatal scalding, severe burns
existing_controls: Boiler licensed operator; gauge glass checked per shift
additional_controls: Valid Chief Inspector of Boilers certificate displayed and diarised for renewal; safety-valve lift test and hydraulic test on schedule with records; low-water cut-out and dual level control proven weekly; lagging survey of all steam and condensate lines with a repair backlog register; blowdown procedure with dedicated PPE and a fixed blowdown vessel
legal_reference: Boilers Act and Rules; BLR 60 & 62 (pressure plant); BLA 62

activity: Boiler internal inspection and tube cleaning
hazard_description: Entry into the boiler shell or furnace with residual heat and oxygen deficiency
potential_consequence: Asphyxiation, heat stroke, burns, entrapment
existing_controls: Entry after shutdown at supervisor's discretion
additional_controls: Confined-space entry permit as a stand-alone permit class; atmospheric testing for O2, CO, and combustibles before and continuously during entry; forced-air ventilation; trained standby attendant with entry log and rescue plan including a tripod and harness; LOTO on fuel, feedwater and steam isolations
legal_reference: BLR 68 (dangerous operations); BLA 62; BLA 79c (health check for dangerous operations)

activity: Handling caustic soda (NaOH) and nitric acid for clean-in-place
hazard_description: Splash, spray-back or mis-connection during chemical dosing, dilution and line connection
potential_consequence: Chemical burns to eyes and skin, permanent blindness, inhalation injury
existing_controls: Gloves issued; chemicals stored in the CIP room
additional_controls: Closed-loop dosing with keyed and colour-coded couplings to prevent mis-connection; segregated and bunded storage of acid and alkali with secondary containment at 110% of the largest vessel; SDS in Bangla and English at the point of use; emergency shower and eye wash within 10 seconds' travel, tested weekly; chemical-splash goggles, face shield, apron and gauntlets specified per task; spill kit and neutralising agent
legal_reference: BLA 62 (dangerous fumes); BLR 68; Environment Conservation Rules 1997

activity: Entry into milk silos, balance tanks and mixing vessels for cleaning or repair
hazard_description: Residual caustic, oxygen deficiency, unexpected agitator start-up, engulfment
potential_consequence: Fatality by asphyxiation or drowning in residual liquid; amputation by agitator
existing_controls: Tank cleaned before entry; buddy present
additional_controls: Confined-space permit with a register of all confined spaces on site and their hazard profile; LOTO on agitator drive, inlet valves and CIP supply, verified by a try-out; gas test and continuous monitoring; harness with retrieval line and a rehearsed rescue plan; annual confined-space rescue drill with FSCD participation

activity: Switching, panel work and fault finding on LV/HV equipment
hazard_description: Electric shock and arc flash from live working, inadequate isolation or missing panel doors
potential_consequence: Electrocution fatality, arc-flash burns, cardiac arrest
existing_controls: Only electricians allowed; rubber mat at some panels
additional_controls: Electrical safety rules with a permit for any work above 415 V; LOTO with proving dead using a proven tester before touching; arc-flash study and labelling of incident energy with matched arc-rated PPE; insulated mats, shrouded terminals and IP-rated enclosures; annual thermographic survey of all panels; competency certification for every electrician
legal_reference: BLR 58 (electrical system certificate); BLA 62; Electricity Act

activity: Uncontrolled temporary and extension wiring in production and packing areas
hazard_description: Overloaded sockets, damaged insulation, joints without junction boxes; ignition source in a dust-classified zone
potential_consequence: Fire origin, electrocution; short circuit is the single largest recorded fire cause nationally (34.71% of 2025 incidents)
existing_controls: Electrician repairs on report
additional_controls: Ban on permanent use of temporary wiring with a 30-day maximum permit; monthly electrical-safety walk with a photographic non-conformance register; RCD/ELCB protection on all portable-tool circuits, tested six-monthly; portable appliance testing programme with pass labels

activity: Welding, grinding and cutting during maintenance and projects
hazard_description: Sparks and hot slag igniting powder dust layers, packaging film, cardboard, oil residue or insulation
potential_consequence: Major fire, business interruption, burn injuries, fatality
existing_controls: Fire extinguisher brought to the job
additional_controls: Hot Work Permit valid for one shift only, with a documented fire watch during work and for 60 minutes afterwards; 11 m clearance or fire blankets over all combustibles; gas test in areas with dust or flammable vapour; alternative cold-cutting methods considered first; permit register reviewed weekly by the HSE Executive
legal_reference: BLA 62; Fire Prevention and Extinction Act 2003 ss.4 & 8; BNBC 2020 Part 4

activity: Work at height on silo tops, roofs, oven platforms and light fittings
hazard_description: Fall from height due to unprotected edges, fragile roof sheets and use of unsuitable ladders
potential_consequence: Fatal fall, spinal injury, permanent disability; falls from height are a leading national fatality cause
existing_controls: Ladders available; workers told to be careful
additional_controls: Work-at-Height Permit above 1.8 m; fixed guardrails and static lines on all silo tops and roof access routes; fragile-roof marking and crawl boards; full-body harness with a double lanyard and a written rescue-from-height plan; ladder register with quarterly inspection tags; mobile elevating work platform for routine high-level lighting work

activity: Forklift and pallet-truck movement around pedestrians
hazard_description: Pedestrian struck by forklift, load falling from forks, rack collision and collapse
potential_consequence: Fatal crush injury, fractures, rack collapse burying personnel
existing_controls: Trained drivers; horn at corners
additional_controls: Physically segregated pedestrian walkways with barriers and marked crossings; site speed limit of 10 km/h with a monitored telematics or key-card system; daily pre-use checklist per truck; blue-spot and reversing alarms; annual racking integrity inspection to a recognised standard with a damage-reporting process; licensed operators only, revalidated every three years

activity: Stacking and de-stacking of finished-goods pallets at height
hazard_description: Falling cases and unstable stacks during retrieval
potential_consequence: Head and crush injuries to pedestrians and operators
existing_controls: Maximum stack height instruction
additional_controls: Load-height limits enforced by rack beam labelling and floor marking; pallet-condition inspection before racking; stretch-wrapping standard specified and audited; hard hats mandatory in the racking aisles; exclusion zone during high-level picking

area: Compressor Room / Packing Hall / Blower Deck
activity: Continuous exposure to plant noise
hazard_description: Noise levels expected above 85 dB(A) at compressors, blowers, packing machines and the fryer extraction fan
potential_consequence: Permanent noise-induced hearing loss, tinnitus, impaired communication in emergencies
existing_controls: Ear plugs available in the store
additional_controls: Octave-band noise survey and a site noise contour map; acoustic enclosures on compressors and blowers as the first control; posted hearing-protection zones with signage; issued and fit-tested hearing protection matched to the measured level; audiometric baseline and annual screening for exposed workers

activity: Work in high radiant-heat zones, especially April to September
hazard_description: Heat stress from ambient temperature above 35 C combined with radiant heat and high humidity
potential_consequence: Heat exhaustion, heat stroke, dehydration, collapse and secondary injury
existing_controls: Drinking water provided
additional_controls: WBGT monitoring at the fryer, oven and boiler with a published work-rest schedule by heat index; insulation of hot surfaces and spot cooling with air movers; electrolyte drinks and an air-conditioned rest area; heat-illness recognition training for supervisors; acclimatisation protocol for new and returning workers

activity: Movement on wet process floors in the milk, CIP and washing areas
hazard_description: Slip on wet, oily or powder-dusted floors; trip on hoses and cables
potential_consequence: Fractures, head injury, sprains; consistently the highest-frequency injury type in food plants
existing_controls: Mopping when noticed
additional_controls: Drainage-gradient survey and repair of ponding areas; anti-slip flooring or coatings in wet zones with a measured pendulum test value; hose-management stations and cable routing above head height; mandatory slip-resistant footwear specified by rating and issued to all process staff; wet-floor signage and a defined cleaning-window schedule

activity: Contractor and project work on site
hazard_description: Contractors working outside the site HSE system without induction, insurance or method statements
potential_consequence: Contractor fatality with full legal liability on the principal employer, uncontrolled introduction of new hazards
existing_controls: Gate pass issued by security
additional_controls: Pre-qualification of contractors on HSE criteria before award; mandatory site induction with a photo ID badge that expires; approved method statement and risk assessment reviewed before mobilisation; permit-to-work applies equally to contractors; daily contractor toolbox talk with attendance record; contractor HSE performance scored and fed back into the vendor list

activity: Emergency evacuation from production and warehouse buildings
hazard_description: Blocked or locked escape routes, insufficient exit width, inadequate assembly control, night-shift staffing gaps
potential_consequence: Mass-casualty event; the RMG sector's fire history in Bangladesh is the reference case for this failure mode
existing_controls: Fire drill conducted occasionally; extinguishers in place
additional_controls: Two independent means of escape from every occupied area, never locked during production, audited weekly; emergency lighting and photoluminescent exit signage tested monthly; fire alarm and detection covering the powder, fryer and warehouse zones; documented evacuation drill at least every three months including one night-shift and one shelter-in-place ammonia drill per year, with timed muster and a formal debrief; trained fire team and first-aiders on every shift with a coverage roster
legal_reference: BLA 62; BLA 89; Fire Prevention and Extinction Act 2003 ss.4 & 8; BNBC 2020 Part 4

activity: First aid and medical response
hazard_description: Insufficient first-aid coverage and no defined route to definitive care for a serious burn, ammonia or crush casualty
potential_consequence: Preventable death or permanent disability from delayed treatment
existing_controls: First-aid box in the office
additional_controls: First-aid boxes to the prescribed scale with a monthly stock check; certified first-aiders on every shift with names posted; burn-specific and ammonia-specific first-aid protocols displayed at the fryer and refrigeration plant; a written arrangement with the nearest burn-capable hospital and a dedicated emergency vehicle on site; injury-response drill twice a year

activity: Effluent treatment plant operation and discharge
hazard_description: Discharge of high-BOD/COD dairy and caustic effluent outside the standards; ETP bypass or overload during peak CIP
potential_consequence: Environmental prosecution, ECC renewal refused, fish kill and community complaint, reputational loss
existing_controls: ETP operated by an operator; occasional testing
additional_controls: Continuous pH and flow monitoring with logging at the discharge point; monthly third-party BOD, COD, TSS and oil-and-grease testing against Environment Conservation Rules 1997 Schedule 10; balancing-tank capacity sized for peak CIP load; interlock preventing discharge outside the permitted pH band; valid Environmental Clearance Certificate tracked for renewal; sludge disposal manifest
legal_reference: Environment Conservation Act 1995; Environment Conservation Rules 1997 (ECC and discharge standards)

activity: Stack emissions and ambient air quality at the plant boundary
hazard_description: Boiler and generator stack emissions of PM, SOx and NOx adding to an already heavily loaded ambient airshed
potential_consequence: Regulatory non-compliance, community exposure, worker exposure at intake points
existing_controls: Stack in place; no monitoring programme
additional_controls: Bi-annual stack monitoring against Environment Conservation Rules 1997 standards; fuel-quality specification and records; boundary PM2.5/PM10 monitoring with results benchmarked against the national ambient dataset; siting of fresh-air intakes away from stack downwash; combustion tuning programme

activity: Ambient particulate exposure of outdoor and yard workers
hazard_description: Ambient PM2.5 in the Dhaka industrial belt regularly exceeds WHO guideline levels, adding to occupational exposure for yard, loading and security staff
potential_consequence: Chronic respiratory and cardiovascular morbidity, absenteeism, reduced fitness for work
additional_controls: Daily AQI-triggered work-adjustment protocol using the site's own PM2.5 feed and the national ambient dataset; scheduling of heavy outdoor work outside the winter peak-pollution window where feasible; enclosed and positively pressurised gatehouse and loading office; respiratory protection issued on high-AQI days for sustained outdoor work; annual respiratory health screening for outdoor-assigned staff

activity: Reporting of hazards, near misses and minor injuries
hazard_description: Under-reporting culture, with fear of blame suppressing near-miss and first-aid reporting
potential_consequence: Loss of the leading-indicator signal, repeat incidents escalating to serious injury
existing_controls: Accidents reported to the supervisor verbally
additional_controls: Anonymous and named reporting channels including a mobile form and physical cards; a published just-culture policy signed by the Managing Director; near-miss target set as a positive KPI rather than a penalty; monthly recognition for the highest-quality report; every report closed out with visible feedback to the reporter within seven days
legal_reference: BLA 80 (notice of accident); BLR 73; Schedule IV(2)

activity: Statutory Safety Committee operation
hazard_description: Safety Committee constituted on paper only, without quarterly meetings, worker parity or closed actions
potential_consequence: Legal non-conformance, loss of worker participation, DIFE enforcement action; 93% of factories in one national study had a committee but functionality was the failure point
existing_controls: Committee formed at registration
additional_controls: Committee reconstituted to BLR 81 with 50:50 worker-management parity and 6-12 members by headcount; minuted quarterly meetings to BLR Schedule IV(3) with a tracked action register; worker representatives nominated by workers, not appointed; annual committee training; minutes posted on the shop-floor notice board in Bangla

activity: Induction and job-specific HSE training
hazard_description: New, transferred and seasonal workers put to work before hazard-specific training, especially at peak production
potential_consequence: Higher injury rate among short-tenure workers, invalid defence in the event of prosecution
existing_controls: Verbal briefing by the supervisor
additional_controls: Training-needs matrix by job role with a competence register; a rule that no worker starts a task before signed-off induction and job-specific training; toolbox talk programme with a rolling annual topic calendar; refresher intervals defined per hazard class; effectiveness verified by observation and not only by attendance signature

activity: Management of change for new plant, products and layout
hazard_description: New lines, chemicals, machinery or layout changes commissioned without a pre-start HSE review
potential_consequence: Reintroduction of controlled hazards, unguarded new machinery, unassessed chemicals entering site
existing_controls: Engineering informs HSE informally
additional_controls: Mandatory management-of-change procedure with an HSE sign-off gate before commissioning; pre-start safety review checklist covering guarding, LOTO points, emergency stops, ventilation and permit needs; new-chemical approval gate requiring an SDS review before purchase; HIRA updated and re-issued within 30 days of any change

activity: Security and access control interaction with safety
hazard_description: Locked or restricted gates during production, unaccounted visitors and drivers during an emergency
potential_consequence: Delayed evacuation, unaccounted persons at muster, delayed FSCD access
existing_controls: Security guards on gates
additional_controls: Visitor and driver register integrated with the muster roll; emergency-release on all security gates with monthly testing; FSCD access route kept clear and marked with a turning circle; joint security-HSE emergency role definition; drivers inducted and held in a designated safe waiting area

activity: Raw-material inbound and finished-goods outbound vehicle movement
hazard_description: Reversing vehicles, unsecured loads, drivers on foot in the yard, tanker connection during unloading
potential_consequence: Fatal pedestrian strike, load-shift injury; transport is the largest single fatality sector nationally at 385 of 802 deaths in 2025
existing_controls: Banksman used sometimes
additional_controls: One-way yard traffic plan with marked reversing bays and fixed banksman positions; wheel chocks and a driver key-retention system during loading and unloading; tanker-unloading procedure with earthing and a connection checklist; driver waiting area outside the manoeuvring zone; yard lighting to a specified lux level for night operations

activity: Occupational hygiene monitoring programme
hazard_description: No baseline quantitative measurement of dust, noise, heat or chemical exposure against which controls can be judged
potential_consequence: Controls selected without evidence, unrecognised over-exposure, no defence at audit
additional_controls: Annual occupational hygiene survey covering respirable and inhalable dust in powder areas, noise dosimetry, WBGT heat, and ammonia and caustic mist spot checks; results compared against national and ACGIH reference values; exposure register by similar exposure group; findings drive the following year's control plan
